extracted.intended_audience: media scholars, news editors, and news-homepage/product designers
extracted.subtask_description: Use agenda-setting theory to guide homepage/story placement so that editorial decisions (placement, repetition, length, timing, cross-outlet convergence) maximize public salience of issues. Applicable to designing editorial and algorithmic homepage strategies that shape audience priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repetition
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues repeated across outlets and across days achieve top-of-mind status. Repetition is itself a marker of newsworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote sustained and repeated coverage across days and across outlets to build public salience; single, one-off items are less likely to shape the agenda. For homepage models, weighting recurrence across time and sources increases an item’s newsworthiness score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Position / Display
rubrics_metrics.description: Front-page placement, lead-story status, and long-form treatment all signal 'this is important.' Editors' display choices function as newsworthiness markers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use placement (e.g., top-of-homepage, lead module) and visual prominence as explicit signals of importance. Measure/display decisions should be treated as both an output and an input to perceived newsworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length
rubrics_metrics.description: Story length contributes to salience; longer treatments mark higher news value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocate longer-form treatments and prominent formats to items intended to be agenda-driving. For algorithms, include story length or depth as a positive feature when predicting salience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time of Coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories covered earliest in a campaign / news cycle anchor the agenda for the rest of the cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize early coverage of emerging issues to 'anchor' the agenda; timing decisions (who covers what first) influence subsequent prominence across outlets and in audience minds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Outlet Convergence
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues covered by all major outlets achieve maximum agenda weight; idiosyncratic coverage is less effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor and, where appropriate, amplify topics that converge across outlets. In homepage strategy, give higher weight to issues showing cross-outlet pickup to leverage their agenda-setting power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awareness Model
rubrics_metrics.description: Media coverage simply makes audiences aware that an issue exists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use coverage to introduce new issues; initial awareness is a distinct contribution of media separate from ranking or perceived prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priorities Model
rubrics_metrics.description: Media coverage shapes the ranking of issues in importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design placement and prominence to intentionally influence audience rankings of importance (e.g., ordering modules by editorial priority).

rubrics_metrics.name: Salience Model
rubrics_metrics.description: Media coverage shapes how prominent an issue feels in audience minds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salience is subjective prominence; optimize visual, contextual, and repeated cues to increase perceived prominence.

rubrics_metrics.name: First-Level Agenda Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Media transfer the salience of objects (which issues, candidates, events to think about).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus homepage curation on which objects to surface to steer audience attention to particular topics or actors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-Level Agenda Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Media transfer the salience of attributes (which features of those objects to think about).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond surfacing topics, emphasize particular attributes (tone, angle, framing, visuals) to shape how audiences evaluate those topics on the homepage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-existing Public Concern
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues already on the public mind get amplified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect existing public concerns (searches, social signals, polling) and prioritize them for further coverage to amplify salience; homepage algorithms should factor audience pre-existing interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-Source Confirmation
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues with multiple sources flagging them rise faster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multi-source corroboration as a signal for elevating coverage; prioritize items that are being reported or flagged by diverse outlets/sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual Newsworthiness (TV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues with strong visuals reach larger TV audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On visual platforms and homepage modules, favor stories with compelling imagery or video to increase reach and perceived importance; visuals act as a medium-specific news value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with Election Cycle
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues that map to candidate positions get more campaign coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During elections, prioritize issues that connect to candidate stances; alignment with campaign stakes increases an issue's agenda potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persistence
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues sustainable over multiple news cycles dominate the agenda.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor topics that can be continually updated and sustained over time for long-term agenda impact; ephemeral items are less likely to dominate the agenda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Display as an Explicit Newsworthiness Signal
rubrics_metrics.description: Where and how a story is placed encodes editorial newsworthiness judgments. A homepage-positioning model can use placement as a target variable for newsworthiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat display/placement not merely as consequence but as measurable signal and optimization objective; use placement both to reflect and to create perceived importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate-level Effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Agenda-setting operates at the population level — even individual stories that lack high news value can become agenda-shaping if reproduced across outlets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider system-level dynamics: measure cross-outlet reproduction and cumulative exposure rather than assessing stories solely in isolation when optimizing homepages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-coverage Justification / Feedback Loop
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an issue is on the public agenda, additional coverage is justified as 'responsive to public interest' — creating a feedback loop with reader metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of and, where appropriate, correct for feedback loops where metrics-driven re-coverage can artificially amplify issues. Design homepage metrics/algorithms to differentiate genuine public concern from self-reinforcing coverage.
